stem.en: A clinic applies respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette to every person with signs of respiratory infection at the point of entry. Classify each action as part of this standard-precautions approach or not part of it.
stem.zh: 某门诊在入口处对所有有呼吸道感染迹象的人实施呼吸卫生和咳嗽礼仪。判断每项措施是否属于这种标准预防措施。

rows.en: Ask about cough and respiratory symptoms during arrival screening
rows.zh: 到达筛查时询问咳嗽和呼吸道症状

rows.en: Offer a mask to a coughing person who can tolerate it
rows.zh: 向能够耐受的咳嗽者提供口罩

rows.en: Provide tissues and hand-hygiene supplies near the entrance
rows.zh: 在入口附近提供纸巾和手卫生用品

rows.en: Seat symptomatic persons apart from others when space permits
rows.zh: 空间允许时让有症状者与他人分开就座

rows.en: Delay urgent assessment until the cough has stopped
rows.zh: 等咳嗽停止后再进行紧急评估

correct.en: Respiratory hygiene includes early identification, source-control masking when tolerated, tissues and hand hygiene, and spatial separation when feasible. Automatically delaying urgent assessment because a person is coughing is not an infection-control measure.
correct.zh: 呼吸卫生包括尽早识别、在可耐受时佩戴口罩进行源头控制、提供纸巾和手卫生，以及在可行时保持空间距离。仅因咳嗽就自动延迟紧急评估并不是感染控制措施。

byChoice.en: Early symptom identification at entry is part of respiratory hygiene.
byChoice.zh: 入口处尽早识别症状属于呼吸卫生。

byChoice.en: Providing a mask for source control is appropriate when tolerated.
byChoice.zh: 在可耐受时提供口罩进行源头控制是适当的。

byChoice.en: Tissues and hand-hygiene supplies reduce contamination from secretions.
byChoice.zh: 纸巾和手卫生用品可减少分泌物污染。

byChoice.en: Separating symptomatic persons when feasible reduces exposure.
byChoice.zh: 在可行时让有症状者保持距离可减少暴露。

byChoice.en: Urgent clinical assessment should not be withheld solely because of cough.
byChoice.zh: 不应仅因咳嗽而延迟紧急临床评估。

sourceMetadata: CDC, Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings, Standard Precautions, https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/core-practices/index.html

stem.en: Floodwater has entered the hospital's ground floor and is rising. The emergency plan directs staff to move clients and essential services from lower floors to predetermined safe floors within the same building. This movement is called ________ evacuation.
stem.zh: 洪水已进入医院一楼并持续上涨。应急计划要求工作人员把患者和关键服务从较低楼层转移到同一建筑内预定的安全楼层。这种转移称为________疏散。

correct.en: Moving occupants between floors within the same building is vertical evacuation.
correct.zh: 在同一建筑内楼层之间转移人员称为垂直疏散。

byChoice.en: “Vertical” describes movement to another floor within the facility.
byChoice.zh: “垂直”描述在机构内转移到另一楼层。

sourceMetadata: ASPR TRACIE, St. Louis Hospital Evacuation and Transportation Plan, vertical evacuation defined as movement to a different floor within the facility, https://files.asprtracie.hhs.gov/documents/st-louis-hospital-evacuation-and-transportation-plan-508.pdf

stem.en: During an active-shooter event, the hospital's emergency plan directs staff in unaffected locked units to secure in place, silence devices, stay away from doors and windows, and wait for an authenticated all-clear. After the all-clear, clinical teams begin triage in the designated safe area. Complete the response.
stem.zh: 医院发生活跃枪手事件时，应急计划要求未受影响且已上锁的病区就地防护、将设备静音、远离门窗，并等待经验证的解除警报。解除警报后，临床团队在指定安全区域开始分诊。完成应对措施。

clozeStem.en: Before the authenticated all-clear, the nurse should {{1}}. After the all-clear, the nurse should {{2}}.
clozeStem.zh: 在收到经验证的解除警报前，护士应{{1}}。解除警报后，护士应{{2}}。

options.en: enter the corridor to look for casualties
options.zh: 进入走廊寻找伤员

options.en: remain secured and avoid opening the door for an unverified voice
options.zh: 保持锁闭，不因未经核实的声音而开门

options.en: announce the unit location over a personal phone
options.zh: 用私人手机公布病区位置

options.en: begin triage in the designated safe area
options.zh: 在指定安全区域开始分诊

options.en: resume routine unit operations without reporting to the designated safe area
options.zh: 不前往指定安全区域报到，直接恢复病区常规运行

options.en: continue lockdown indefinitely without checking instructions
options.zh: 无限期继续封锁且不查看指示

correct.en: Before an authenticated all-clear, the unit follows secure-in-place actions and does not open the door for an unverified voice. After the all-clear, staff transition to clinical triage in the designated safe area; resuming routine operations would skip the plan's post-event response.
correct.zh: 在收到经验证的解除警报前，病区应执行就地防护措施，不因未经核实的声音而开门。解除警报后，工作人员转入指定安全区域开展临床分诊；直接恢复常规运行会跳过计划规定的事件后应对。

byChoice.en: The plan explicitly requires secure-in-place behavior before the all-clear.
byChoice.zh: 计划明确要求在解除警报前就地防护。

byChoice.en: The plan directs clinical triage only after the authenticated all-clear.
byChoice.zh: 计划要求仅在经验证的解除警报后开展临床分诊。

sourceMetadata: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, Hospitals and Healthcare Facilities Security Action Guide, lockdown, safe-location, patient-security, and device-silencing guidance, https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/publications/19_0515_cisa_action-guide-hospitals-and-healthcare.pdf; the authenticated all-clear and post-event sequence are supplied by the facility plan in the item

stem.en: A capable adult enrolled in a clinical study says before the next study-only intervention, “I want to leave the study.” Staff imply that withdrawing could affect ordinary clinical care. Highlight the nursing statements and actions that honor the client's decision.
stem.zh: 一名具有决策能力、参加临床研究的成年患者在下一项仅用于研究的干预前说：“我想退出这项研究。”工作人员暗示退出可能会影响常规临床护理。请标出尊重患者决定的护理表述和行动。

segments.en: The nurse states that participation is voluntary and that withdrawing will not reduce ordinary clinical care.
segments.zh: 护士说明参加研究是自愿的，退出研究不会减少常规临床护理。

segments.en: The nurse asks the client to complete the next study-only intervention before withdrawal can take effect.
segments.zh: 护士要求患者先完成下一项仅用于研究的干预，退出才会生效。

segments.en: The nurse stops further research-only interactions and interventions now.
segments.zh: 护士立即停止后续仅用于研究的接触和干预。

segments.en: The nurse promptly notifies the research team of the client's withdrawal.
segments.zh: 护士立即通知研究团队患者已决定退出。

segments.en: The nurse follows the study process for documenting the withdrawal while continuing clinically indicated care.
segments.zh: 护士按研究流程记录退出决定，同时继续提供临床上需要的护理。

segments.en: The nurse warns that the clinical team may reconsider routine treatment if the client leaves the study.
segments.zh: 护士警告患者，如果退出研究，临床团队可能会重新考虑常规治疗。

segments.en: The nurse continues study follow-up calls until the sponsor approves the withdrawal.
segments.zh: 护士继续进行研究随访电话，直到研究申办方批准退出。

segments.en: The nurse separates the research decision from the client's ongoing therapeutic relationship with the care team.
segments.zh: 护士将退出研究的决定与患者和医疗团队之间持续的治疗关系区分开来。

correct.en: A capable participant may withdraw without penalty or loss of benefits. Once the client withdraws, research-only interactions and interventions stop, the research team is notified, and ordinary clinical care continues.
correct.zh: 具有决策能力的研究参与者可以退出，不应受到惩罚或失去应有利益。患者退出后，应停止仅用于研究的接触和干预，通知研究团队，并继续常规临床护理。

byChoice.en: This directly protects voluntary withdrawal without loss of ordinary care.
byChoice.zh: 这直接保障患者可自愿退出，且不会失去常规护理。

byChoice.en: Withdrawal does not depend on completing another research-only intervention.
byChoice.zh: 退出研究不以完成另一项仅用于研究的干预为条件。

byChoice.en: Further research-only interaction or intervention must stop when the client withdraws.
byChoice.zh: 患者退出后，必须停止后续仅用于研究的接触或干预。

byChoice.en: Promptly notifying the research team allows the withdrawal to be implemented and documented.
byChoice.zh: 及时通知研究团队可落实并记录退出决定。

byChoice.en: Documenting the withdrawal while continuing clinically indicated care preserves both the record and the therapeutic relationship.
byChoice.zh: 在继续临床所需护理的同时记录退出决定，既保证记录完整，也维护治疗关系。

byChoice.en: Linking routine treatment to research participation is coercive and contradicts withdrawal without penalty.
byChoice.zh: 把常规治疗与研究参与挂钩具有胁迫性，违反无惩罚退出原则。

byChoice.en: Research follow-up cannot continue merely while awaiting sponsor approval after the participant has withdrawn from research interactions.
byChoice.zh: 参与者已退出研究接触后，不能仅因等待申办方批准而继续研究随访。

byChoice.en: Research participation is distinct from the client's right to ongoing ordinary clinical care.
byChoice.zh: 研究参与不同于患者继续接受常规临床护理的权利。

sourceMetadata: 45 CFR § 46.116(b)(8), voluntary participation and the right to discontinue without penalty or loss of benefits, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title45-vol1-sec46-116.pdf; HHS Office for Human Research Protections (OHRP), Withdrawal of Subjects from Research Guidance, Guidance A—discontinuing research interactions, interventions, and collection of additional identifiable private information, https://www.hhs.gov/ohrp/regulations-and-policy/guidance/guidance-on-withdrawal-of-subject/index.html

stem.en: A stable medical-surgical inpatient uses a trained service dog that alerts to impending seizures. Classify each proposed staff action. Under the ADA, when the dog's task is not obvious, staff may ask only whether the dog is required because of a disability and what work or task it has been trained to perform. Staff may not demand certification or a task demonstration. The handler is responsible for the animal's care. Exclusion is permitted only for a specific allowed reason, such as a dog being out of control and the handler not taking effective action.
stem.zh: 一名病情稳定的内外科住院患者使用一只经过训练、可预警即将发生癫痫发作的服务犬。请对每项拟议的工作人员行动进行分类。根据 ADA，当服务犬的任务并不明显时，工作人员只能询问该犬是否因残障而需要，以及它受过训练可执行什么工作或任务。工作人员不得要求出示认证或让犬现场演示任务。服务犬的照护由其引导者负责。只有在特定允许理由下，例如服务犬失控且引导者未采取有效纠正措施时，才可将其排除。

rows.en: Allow the service dog to remain with the client in ordinary patient areas.
rows.zh: 允许服务犬在普通患者区域陪伴患者。

rows.en: If the task is not obvious, ask the two permitted questions described in the stem.
rows.zh: 如果服务犬的任务并不明显，询问题干中说明的两个允许问题。

rows.en: Require an official service-animal certificate before the dog may stay.
rows.zh: 要求先出示官方服务动物认证，服务犬才可以留下。

rows.en: Ask the client to have the dog demonstrate its seizure-alert task.
rows.zh: 要求患者让服务犬现场演示癫痫预警任务。

rows.en: Let the client arrange feeding, toileting, and other routine care for the dog.
rows.zh: 由患者安排服务犬的喂食、排泄和其他日常照护。

rows.en: If the dog becomes uncontrolled and the handler does not correct it, remove the dog while continuing to offer the client care without the animal present.
rows.zh: 如果服务犬失控且引导者没有纠正，可将犬带离，同时在服务犬不在场的情况下继续为患者提供护理。

correct.en: Advocacy means facilitating the trained service dog's access, limiting inquiries to the two ADA-permitted questions when needed, avoiding documentation or demonstration demands, respecting the handler's responsibility for animal care, and using exclusion only for a permitted, individualized reason.
correct.zh: 维护患者权益包括允许经过训练的服务犬进入、必要时只询问 ADA 允许的两个问题、不要求证明或演示、尊重引导者负责动物照护，并且只在有允许的个别化理由时排除服务犬。

byChoice.en: A service dog generally accompanies its handler in areas open to patients.
byChoice.zh: 服务犬通常可以陪同引导者进入向患者开放的区域。

byChoice.en: These are the only two questions permitted when the service task is not apparent.
byChoice.zh: 当服务犬的任务不明显时，只允许询问这两个问题。

byChoice.en: The ADA does not require service-dog certification or documentation as a condition of access.
byChoice.zh: ADA 不要求以服务犬认证或证明作为进入条件。

byChoice.en: Staff may not require the dog to demonstrate its trained task.
byChoice.zh: 工作人员不得要求服务犬现场演示其受训任务。

byChoice.en: The handler, not hospital staff, is responsible for feeding, toileting, and supervising the dog.
byChoice.zh: 服务犬的喂食、排泄和看护由引导者负责，而不是由医院工作人员负责。

byChoice.en: Loss of control that the handler does not correct is a permitted reason for removal; the client must still be offered services without the dog.
byChoice.zh: 服务犬失控且引导者未纠正属于允许排除的理由；即使犬被带离，仍必须继续向患者提供服务。

sourceMetadata: U.S. Department of Justice, Frequently Asked Questions about Service Animals and the ADA, Q7, Q9, Q14-Q15, Q17, Q25, and Q28, https://www.ada.gov/resources/service-animals-faqs/

stem.en: Two potassium specimens have hemolyzed. Nursing and laboratory staff blame one another at the bedside while the repeat result needed for a treatment decision is delayed. The client is currently stable. Complete the bow-tie to identify the problem, the two best actions, and the two measures of closure.
stem.zh: 两份血钾标本均发生溶血。护理人员和检验人员在床旁互相指责，而治疗决策所需的复查结果被延误。患者目前病情稳定。请完成蝴蝶结图，确定问题、两项最佳行动和两项闭环指标。

condition.en: Client refusal of repeat specimen collection
condition.zh: 患者拒绝再次采集标本

condition.en: Unresolved interdepartmental conflict delaying necessary clinical data
condition.zh: 未解决的跨部门冲突正在延误必要的临床数据

condition.en: Confirmed acute hyperkalemia requiring immediate treatment
condition.zh: 已确诊的急性高钾血症，需要立即治疗

actions.en: Have both departments collect separate specimens to determine which team is at fault
actions.zh: 让两个部门分别采集标本，以确定哪一方有责任

actions.en: Hold a brief nursing-laboratory huddle away from the bedside and name the shared goal
actions.zh: 离开床旁进行简短的护理—检验科协调会，并明确共同目标

actions.en: Wait for both department managers to investigate before recollecting the specimen
actions.zh: 等待两个部门的管理者完成调查后再重新采集标本

actions.en: Agree on an objective collection, labeling, and transport plan with named roles and a time target
actions.zh: 就客观的采集、标识和运送方案达成一致，并明确责任人和时间目标

parameters.en: Repeat potassium result is posted and communicated to the treatment team
parameters.zh: 复查血钾结果已发布并传达给治疗团队

parameters.en: The agreed nursing-laboratory communication loop is completed with a named receiver
parameters.zh: 约定的护理—检验科沟通闭环已完成，并有明确的接收者

parameters.en: The number of complaint emails sent about the incident
parameters.zh: 围绕该事件发送的投诉邮件数量

parameters.en: One department accepts responsibility for both hemolyzed specimens
parameters.zh: 其中一个部门承担两份溶血标本的责任

correct.en: The immediate management issue is unresolved interdepartmental conflict delaying a needed repeat result. A brief huddle and an objective shared plan restore coordinated work. Closure requires both the clinical result and completion of the agreed communication loop.
correct.zh: 当前的管理问题是未解决的跨部门冲突延误了所需的复查结果。简短协调会和客观的共同方案可恢复协作。闭环既需要得到临床结果，也需要完成约定的沟通流程。

byChoice.en: This condition captures the actual delay and team-process failure while the client remains stable.
byChoice.zh: 该病情描述准确反映了患者稳定时存在的延误和团队流程失效。

byChoice.en: No valid potassium result confirms hyperkalemia, so treatment cannot be keyed to an unverified diagnosis.
byChoice.zh: 目前没有有效血钾结果证实高钾血症，因此不能以未经证实的诊断作为答案。

byChoice.en: The scenario does not state that the client refused recollection.
byChoice.zh: 情境中没有说明患者拒绝重新采集标本。

byChoice.en: A brief huddle de-escalates blame and rapidly aligns the two departments around the client's need.
byChoice.zh: 简短协调会可缓和指责，使两个部门迅速围绕患者需要达成一致。

byChoice.en: A shared, objective plan addresses the collection-to-result pathway that has failed twice.
byChoice.zh: 共同、客观的方案直接处理已连续两次失败的采集到出结果流程。

byChoice.en: Waiting for a full managerial investigation unnecessarily prolongs the clinical delay.
byChoice.zh: 等待完整管理调查会不必要地延长临床延误。

byChoice.en: Duplicate collections designed to assign blame waste resources and do not represent a shared resolution plan.
byChoice.zh: 为了追责而重复采集会浪费资源，也不是共同解决方案。

byChoice.en: The needed result reaching the treatment team is essential evidence that the clinical delay has closed.
byChoice.zh: 所需结果到达治疗团队是临床延误已闭环的关键证据。

byChoice.en: Closed-loop communication confirms that the agreed update was received rather than merely sent.
byChoice.zh: 闭环沟通可确认约定的更新已被接收，而不只是已发送。

byChoice.en: Assigning blame is not a clinical or teamwork closure measure.
byChoice.zh: 追究责任不是临床或团队闭环指标。

byChoice.en: Complaint volume does not show that the repeat result or communication process was completed.
byChoice.zh: 投诉数量不能证明复查结果或沟通流程已完成。

sourceMetadata: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Two-Day Training Content, Team Leadership module, Monitoring and Modifying the Plan—Huddle (Slide 31) and Facilitating Conflict Resolution and Teamwork (Slide 34), https://www.ahrq.gov/teamstepps-program/curriculum/team/teach/two-day.html

stem.en: An alert client was informed about the hospital directory and explicitly opted out. A caller asks whether the client is admitted and requests the room number.
stem.zh: 一名神志清醒的患者已被告知医院名录的相关规定，并明确选择不加入名录。一名来电者询问该患者是否住院，并索要房间号。

clozeStem.zh: 工作人员应当{{q05_d1}}，并且应当{{q05_d2}}。

options.en: confirm admission but withhold the room number
options.zh: 确认患者已住院，但不提供房间号

options.en: not confirm the client's presence or location
options.zh: 不确认患者是否在院或其所在位置

options.en: provide the room number after asking the caller's relationship
options.zh: 询问来电者与患者的关系后提供房间号

options.en: use the usual directory response because the caller knows the client's name
options.zh: 因为来电者知道患者姓名，所以按通常名录流程回答

options.en: follow the client's directory restriction
options.zh: 遵守患者的名录限制

options.en: transfer the caller to the nursing unit for confirmation
options.zh: 把来电转接到护理单元进行确认

correct.en: A client who opts out of the facility directory has restricted disclosure of directory information. Staff must not confirm that the client is present or disclose the room location and must follow the documented restriction.
correct.zh: 选择退出医院名录的患者已限制名录信息披露。工作人员不得确认患者是否在院，也不得透露房间位置，并必须遵守已记录的限制。

byChoice.en: The correct completion is not to confirm presence or location. Confirming admission still discloses directory information, and a caller's claimed relationship does not override the opt-out.
byChoice.zh: 正确填项是不确认患者是否在院或其位置。即使不提供房间号，确认住院仍会披露名录信息；来电者声称的关系也不能推翻退出决定。

byChoice.en: The correct completion is to follow the directory restriction. Knowing the client's name or transferring the call does not authorize disclosure.
byChoice.zh: 正确填项是遵守名录限制。知道患者姓名或转接电话都不能授权披露。

sourceMetadata: HHS Office for Civil Rights, HIPAA FAQ 483, facility directory opt-out under 45 CFR 164.510(a), https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/483/does-hipaa-permit-hospitals-to-inform-visitors-about-a-patients-location/index.html

stem.en: A nursing-station whiteboard is directly visible from a public elevator lobby. Facility policy permits only client initials and operational bed status on a whiteboard that is shielded from public view. Highlight the entries and placement facts that violate the stated safeguards.
stem.zh: 护理站白板可从公共电梯大厅直接看到。机构政策只允许在不被公众看到的白板上记录患者姓名首字母和床位运行状态。请标出违反上述保护措施的内容和放置事实。

segments.en: The whiteboard faces the public elevator lobby and can be read from there.
segments.zh: 白板朝向公共电梯大厅，从那里可以读到内容。

segments.en: It lists each client's full name.
segments.zh: 白板列出每位患者的完整姓名。

segments.en: It lists room numbers next to the names.
segments.zh: 白板在姓名旁列出房间号。

segments.en: It lists specific diagnoses such as “pancreatic cancer” and “HIV infection.”
segments.zh: 白板列出“胰腺癌”和“HIV 感染”等具体诊断。

segments.en: A shielded staff-only board uses client initials.
segments.zh: 一块仅供工作人员查看、已遮挡公众视线的白板使用患者姓名首字母。

segments.en: The shielded staff-only board shows operational status such as “bed ready.”
segments.zh: 仅供工作人员查看、已遮挡的白板显示“床位已准备”等运行状态。

correct.en: HIPAA does not make every nursing-station whiteboard inherently prohibited, but reasonable safeguards are required. Under the stated facility policy, public visibility and the use of full names, room numbers, and diagnoses violate the allowed, shielded initials-and-bed-status format.
correct.zh: HIPAA 并非一概禁止护理站白板，但必须采取合理保护措施。根据题干中的机构政策，公众可见，以及使用完整姓名、房间号和具体诊断，都违反了仅允许在遮挡白板上使用姓名首字母和床位状态的规定。

byChoice.en: Direct readability from a public lobby defeats the required safeguard against public viewing.
byChoice.zh: 从公共大厅可直接读到内容，违反了防止公众查看的保护要求。

byChoice.en: Full names exceed the policy's permitted use of initials.
byChoice.zh: 完整姓名超出政策允许使用姓名首字母的范围。

byChoice.en: Room numbers are not among the policy's permitted whiteboard entries.
byChoice.zh: 房间号不属于该政策允许记录在白板上的内容。

byChoice.en: Specific diagnoses are more detailed than the permitted operational bed-status information.
byChoice.zh: 具体诊断比政策允许的床位运行状态信息更为敏感和详细。

byChoice.en: Initials on a shielded staff-only board fit the stated safeguard.
byChoice.zh: 在仅供工作人员查看且已遮挡的白板上使用姓名首字母符合题干保护措施。

byChoice.en: Operational bed status on the shielded board is explicitly permitted by the facility policy.
byChoice.zh: 机构政策明确允许在已遮挡白板上显示床位运行状态。

sourceMetadata: HHS Office for Civil Rights, HIPAA FAQ 200, reasonable safeguards for nursing-station whiteboards and public visibility, https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/200/what-safeguards-are-needed-to-continue-practices/index.html

stem.en: A client receiving maintenance hemodialysis is relocating and is due for the next treatment within 48 hours. A possible receiving center has been named, but acceptance and chair time are unconfirmed. The dialysis prescription, last treatment record, vascular-access information, recent laboratory results, and medication list have not been transmitted. Complete the bow-tie.
stem.zh: 一名接受维持性血液透析的患者即将搬迁，并需在 48 小时内接受下一次治疗。虽然已提出一个可能接收的透析中心，但尚未确认接收资格和透析时段。透析处方、上次治疗记录、血管通路信息、近期检验结果和用药清单均未传送。请完成蝴蝶结图。

condition.en: Unsafe dialysis transition with no confirmed receiving appointment or clinical handoff
condition.zh: 透析转衔不安全：未确认接收预约，也未完成临床交接

condition.en: Routine relocation with a fully established dialysis schedule
condition.zh: 常规搬迁，透析安排已完全落实

condition.en: Client refusal of the next dialysis treatment
condition.zh: 患者拒绝下一次透析治疗

actions.en: Discharge the client with the center's phone number and ask the client to secure a chair after moving
actions.zh: 让患者带着透析中心电话号码出院，并要求其搬家后自行安排透析时段

actions.en: Transmit only the medication list because the receiving center can reconstruct the dialysis prescription later
actions.zh: 只发送用药清单，因为接收中心之后可以重新制定透析处方

actions.en: Contact the receiving center and confirm acceptance with a specific treatment date and chair time
actions.zh: 联系接收中心，确认其接收患者，并确定具体治疗日期和透析时段

actions.en: Send the dialysis prescription, last treatment record, access information, recent laboratory results, and medication list to the responsible receiving team
actions.zh: 向接收团队发送透析处方、上次治疗记录、通路信息、近期检验结果和用药清单

parameters.en: The client has purchased a home scale
parameters.zh: 患者已购买家用体重秤

parameters.en: The receiving team confirms receipt of the clinical handoff and readiness to provide the next treatment
parameters.zh: 接收团队确认已收到临床交接资料，并已准备好提供下一次治疗

parameters.en: The client has a general transportation brochure
parameters.zh: 患者拿到一份一般交通信息手册

parameters.en: Receiving-center acceptance, date, and chair time are documented and understood by the client
parameters.zh: 接收中心的接收确认、日期和透析时段已记录，患者也已理解

correct.en: The client has an unsafe transition because the next dialysis treatment and the clinical handoff are not secured. The nurse coordinates confirmed acceptance and chair time and transmits the information needed for safe follow-up. Closure requires documented appointment details and confirmation that the receiving team has the handoff and can provide treatment.
correct.zh: 患者的转衔不安全，因为下一次透析治疗和临床交接尚未落实。护士应协调确认接收和透析时段，并传送安全后续治疗所需的信息。闭环需要记录预约细节，并确认接收团队已收到交接资料且能够提供治疗。

byChoice.en: This identifies both missing elements: a confirmed treatment appointment and the information needed by the receiving team.
byChoice.zh: 该选项同时指出两个缺失环节：已确认的治疗预约和接收团队所需的信息。

byChoice.en: The schedule is not established; acceptance and chair time remain unconfirmed.
byChoice.zh: 透析安排尚未落实；接收资格和透析时段仍未确认。

byChoice.en: The scenario describes a coordination failure, not treatment refusal.
byChoice.zh: 情境描述的是协调失败，而不是患者拒绝治疗。

byChoice.en: A named possible center is insufficient until it accepts the client and assigns a specific treatment time.
byChoice.zh: 仅提出一个可能的中心并不够，必须由该中心确认接收并安排具体治疗时间。

byChoice.en: These records allow the receiving team to continue the prescribed dialysis safely and understand the access, recent treatment, laboratory, and medication context.
byChoice.zh: 这些资料可使接收团队安全延续透析处方，并了解通路、近期治疗、检验和用药情况。

byChoice.en: Making the client arrange the appointment after relocation risks missing a time-sensitive treatment.
byChoice.zh: 让患者搬迁后自行安排预约，可能导致错过时间敏感的治疗。

byChoice.en: The medication list alone omits essential dialysis and access information.
byChoice.zh: 仅有用药清单会遗漏关键的透析和血管通路信息。

byChoice.en: A documented, understood chair time proves that the next treatment is actually scheduled.
byChoice.zh: 已记录且患者理解的透析时段，证明下一次治疗确已安排。

byChoice.en: Receipt and readiness confirmation closes the provider-to-provider handoff loop.
byChoice.zh: 确认资料已接收且可提供治疗，完成了医疗团队之间的交接闭环。

byChoice.en: A transportation brochure may be useful but does not prove that dialysis is arranged.
byChoice.zh: 交通手册可能有帮助，但不能证明透析已安排。

byChoice.en: A home scale does not establish receiving-center acceptance or treatment continuity.
byChoice.zh: 家用体重秤不能证明接收中心已接收患者或治疗已连续衔接。

sourceMetadata: 42 CFR § 494.170(d), transfer of requested dialysis medical-record information to the receiving facility, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-G/part-494/subpart-E/section-494.170; National Kidney Foundation, Traveling While on Dialysis—arranging destination appointments and transmitting treatment dates, prescription, recent treatment records, access information, laboratory results, and medication information, https://www.kidney.org/news-stories/traveling-while-dialysis-start-here

stem.en: A client with a documented prior diagnosis of bulimia nervosa receives a new order for bupropion XL.
stem.zh: 一名病历中记录有既往神经性贪食症诊断的患者收到新的 bupropion XL 医嘱。

clozeStem.en: The nurse should {{q09_d1}} because a current or prior diagnosis of bulimia nervosa is {{q09_d2}} associated with increased seizure risk.
clozeStem.zh: 护士应当{{q09_d1}}，因为当前或既往神经性贪食症诊断是与癫痫发作风险增加相关的{{q09_d2}}。

options.en: administer the dose with food
options.zh: 随餐给予该剂量

options.en: withhold the dose and clarify the order
options.zh: 暂不给药并澄清医嘱

options.en: administer one-half of the ordered XL tablet
options.zh: 给予医嘱 XL 片剂的一半

options.en: a labeled contraindication
options.zh: 药品说明书列明的禁忌证

options.en: an indication for dose escalation
options.zh: 增加剂量的适应证

options.en: a minor administration precaution
options.zh: 轻微的给药注意事项

correct.en: Bupropion XL is contraindicated in clients with a current or prior diagnosis of bulimia nervosa because a higher incidence of seizures has been observed. The nurse should withhold the new dose and clarify the order rather than modifying or administering it.
correct.zh: Bupropion XL 禁用于当前或既往诊断为神经性贪食症的患者，因为此类患者使用该药时观察到更高的癫痫发作发生率。护士应暂不给予新医嘱剂量并澄清医嘱，而不是自行修改或给药。

byChoice.en: The correct action is to withhold and clarify. Food does not remove the contraindication, and an XL tablet should not be halved as an improvised risk-reduction strategy.
byChoice.zh: 正确行动是暂不给药并澄清。随餐不能消除禁忌证，也不能把 XL 片剂减半作为临时降低风险的方法。

byChoice.en: The correct classification is a labeled contraindication. It is not a minor precaution or a reason to increase the dose.
byChoice.zh: 正确分类是药品说明书列明的禁忌证，而不是轻微注意事项或增加剂量的理由。

sourceMetadata: DailyMed, Bupropion Hydrochloride Extended-Release Tablets (XL) prescribing information, Contraindications (4) and Warnings and Precautions—Seizure Risk (5.3), https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/getFile.cfm?setid=080853c0-fcab-4645-9ddc-4946e895ac5f&type=pdf

stem.en: Sacubitril/valsartan is due now for a client with heart failure. The medication record shows the last lisinopril dose was given 12 hours ago. The client has no current angioedema and is hemodynamically stable. Complete the bow-tie.
stem.zh: 一名心力衰竭患者现在应使用 sacubitril/valsartan。用药记录显示最后一次 lisinopril 给药是在 12 小时前。患者目前没有血管性水肿，血流动力学稳定。请完成蝴蝶结图。

condition.en: Unsafe ACE-inhibitor-to-ARNI transition before the required washout is complete
condition.zh: ACE 抑制剂转换为 ARNI 的过程不安全：规定的洗脱期尚未完成

condition.en: An isolated ACE-inhibitor cough requiring immediate ARNI administration
condition.zh: 单纯 ACE 抑制剂咳嗽，需要立即给予 ARNI

condition.en: Expected ARNI initiation after a complete ACE-inhibitor washout
condition.zh: ACE 抑制剂洗脱期完成后按预期开始 ARNI

actions.en: Administer the full dose now and monitor only for cough
actions.zh: 现在给予全剂量，并只监测咳嗽

actions.en: Establish at least a 36-hour interval from the last lisinopril dose to the first sacubitril/valsartan dose
actions.zh: 确保从最后一次 lisinopril 到第一次 sacubitril/valsartan 至少间隔 36 小时

actions.en: Give one-half of the sacubitril/valsartan dose now to shorten the washout
actions.zh: 现在给予一半 sacubitril/valsartan 剂量，以缩短洗脱期

actions.en: Hold the sacubitril/valsartan dose and clarify the transition order
actions.zh: 暂缓 sacubitril/valsartan，并澄清转换医嘱

parameters.en: Serum lipase after every dose
parameters.zh: 每次给药后检测血清脂肪酶

parameters.en: Severity of a dry cough as the only safety endpoint
parameters.zh: 仅把干咳严重程度作为安全终点

parameters.en: Facial, lip, tongue, or airway swelling consistent with angioedema
parameters.zh: 符合血管性水肿的面部、嘴唇、舌头或气道肿胀

parameters.en: Blood pressure and clinical tolerance, including dizziness or symptomatic hypotension
parameters.zh: 血压和临床耐受性，包括头晕或症状性低血压

correct.en: Sacubitril/valsartan must not be administered within 36 hours of an ACE inhibitor. At 12 hours, the nurse holds and clarifies the dose and ensures the full washout. After safe initiation, angioedema and blood-pressure tolerance are key monitoring concerns.
correct.zh: Sacubitril/valsartan 不得在使用 ACE 抑制剂后的 36 小时内给药。仅间隔 12 小时时，护士应暂缓并澄清医嘱，确保完成整个洗脱期。安全开始用药后，应重点监测血管性水肿和血压耐受性。

byChoice.en: Only 12 hours have elapsed, so the labeled 36-hour ACE-inhibitor washout is incomplete.
byChoice.zh: 仅过去 12 小时，说明书要求的 36 小时 ACE 抑制剂洗脱期尚未完成。

byChoice.en: This would be true only after at least 36 hours, not at the current 12-hour interval.
byChoice.zh: 只有至少间隔 36 小时才符合此描述，而目前仅间隔 12 小时。

byChoice.en: The load-bearing problem is the unsafe transition timing, not a cough syndrome.
byChoice.zh: 关键问题是转换时间不安全，而不是咳嗽综合征。

byChoice.en: Holding and clarifying prevents administration during a contraindicated overlap interval.
byChoice.zh: 暂缓并澄清可防止在禁忌的重叠时段给药。

byChoice.en: The label requires a 36-hour interval when switching from an ACE inhibitor to sacubitril/valsartan.
byChoice.zh: 药品说明书要求从 ACE 抑制剂转换为 sacubitril/valsartan 时至少间隔 36 小时。

byChoice.en: A reduced dose does not make an incomplete washout safe.
byChoice.zh: 减量不能使未完成的洗脱期变得安全。

byChoice.en: Full-dose administration at 12 hours violates the labeled interval, and cough-only monitoring misses the major risk.
byChoice.zh: 在 12 小时给全剂量违反说明书间隔要求，而且只监测咳嗽会遗漏主要风险。

byChoice.en: Angioedema can compromise the airway and is a labeled serious risk.
byChoice.zh: 血管性水肿可危及气道，是说明书列出的严重风险。

byChoice.en: Sacubitril/valsartan lowers blood pressure and can cause symptomatic hypotension, so clinical tolerance must be assessed.
byChoice.zh: Sacubitril/valsartan 会降低血压并可引起症状性低血压，因此必须评估临床耐受性。

byChoice.en: Cough is not the sole or primary safety endpoint for this transition.
byChoice.zh: 咳嗽不是此次转换唯一或主要的安全监测终点。

byChoice.en: Routine lipase testing after every dose is unrelated to the labeled transition risk.
byChoice.zh: 每次给药后常规检测脂肪酶与说明书所述转换风险无关。

sourceMetadata: DailyMed, ENTRESTO (sacubitril/valsartan) prescribing information, Dosage and Administration 2.1, Contraindications 4, Warnings and Precautions 5.2 Angioedema and 5.3 Hypotension, https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=14bfc60a-9ddf-cac7-e063-6294a90a597b

stem.en: After a mass-casualty incident, several unidentified clients arrive while families and media crowd the entrance. The activated hospital plan requires temporary unique identifiers, a continuously updated patient-tracking list, a designated family-reunification channel, and media release only through the public-information function. Highlight the actions consistent with this plan.
stem.zh: 大规模伤亡事件后，多名身份不明的患者到达医院，家属和媒体挤在入口处。已启动的医院计划要求使用临时唯一标识、持续更新患者追踪清单、设立指定的家属团聚渠道，并且只能通过公共信息职能发布媒体信息。请标出符合该计划的行动。

segments.en: Assign each unidentified client a separate temporary unique identifier.
segments.zh: 为每名身份不明的患者分别分配一个临时唯一标识。

segments.en: Maintain one continuously updated patient-tracking list as clients move through the hospital.
segments.zh: 患者在院内转移时，持续更新同一份患者追踪清单。

segments.en: Route family inquiries to the designated reunification channel.
segments.zh: 将家属查询引导至指定的团聚渠道。

segments.en: Refer media requests to the hospital's public-information function.
segments.zh: 把媒体请求转交医院的公共信息职能处理。

segments.en: Use the same “Unknown Client” identifier for all unidentified arrivals until names are learned.
segments.zh: 在查明姓名前，对所有身份不明的到院者使用同一个“未知患者”标识。

segments.en: Post unidentified-client photographs on the hospital's public social-media account to speed identification.
segments.zh: 在医院公开社交媒体账号上发布身份不明患者的照片，以加快身份确认。

segments.en: Let bedside staff give reporters unverified casualty details to reduce crowding.
segments.zh: 让床旁工作人员向记者提供未经核实的伤亡信息，以减少拥挤。

segments.en: Allow families to search treatment areas independently rather than using the reunification channel.
segments.zh: 允许家属自行进入治疗区域寻找患者，而不是使用团聚渠道。

correct.en: The activated plan creates controlled identity, tracking, family, and media pathways. Unique temporary identifiers and a current tracking list reduce misidentification; family inquiries and public information are routed through their designated functions.
correct.zh: 已启动的计划建立了受控的身份、追踪、家属和媒体信息通道。临时唯一标识和最新追踪清单可减少身份错误；家属查询和公共信息分别通过指定职能处理。

byChoice.en: A separate temporary identifier preserves each unidentified client's identity until reconciliation.
byChoice.zh: 分别使用临时标识可在正式身份核对前保持每名患者身份的独立性。

byChoice.en: Continuous tracking supports location awareness and later identity reconciliation.
byChoice.zh: 持续追踪有助于掌握患者位置并在之后完成身份核对。

byChoice.en: The designated reunification channel centralizes family matching and protects treatment areas.
byChoice.zh: 指定团聚渠道可集中处理家属匹配，并保护治疗区域。

byChoice.en: The plan assigns media release to the public-information function, not bedside staff.
byChoice.zh: 该计划把媒体信息发布交给公共信息职能，而不是床旁工作人员。

byChoice.en: A shared identifier would merge records and create a serious misidentification risk.
byChoice.zh: 多人共用同一标识会混淆记录，并造成严重身份错误风险。

byChoice.en: Public posting bypasses the designated reunification and information-management process.
byChoice.zh: 公开发布照片绕过了指定的团聚和信息管理流程。

byChoice.en: Unverified bedside disclosure violates the designated information-management process and may spread misinformation.
byChoice.zh: 床旁披露未经核实的信息违反指定的信息管理流程，也可能传播错误信息。

byChoice.en: Independent searching increases congestion and bypasses the designated family-reunification process.
byChoice.zh: 家属自行搜索会增加拥挤，并绕过指定团聚流程。

sourceMetadata: ASPR TRACIE, Hospital Mass Casualty Incident Response Plan Considerations, Sections 4 Registration and Documentation, 9 Family Support, and 10 Information Management, https://files.asprtracie.hhs.gov/documents/aspr-tracie-mci-response-plan-considerations.pdf

stem.en: A professional-use blood glucose meter was shared across four clients without cleaning and disinfection between uses. The facility's exposure-response process requires infection-prevention notification and tracing of every potentially exposed client. Complete the bow-tie.
stem.zh: 一台专业用途血糖仪在四名患者之间共用，但每次使用后均未清洁和消毒。机构的暴露应对流程要求通知感染预防部门，并追踪每一名可能暴露的患者。请完成蝴蝶结图。

condition.en: A medication-dosing error affecting only the fourth client
condition.zh: 只影响第四名患者的用药剂量错误

condition.en: Potential bloodborne cross-transmission and client exposure from an improperly shared meter
condition.zh: 血糖仪共用不当导致潜在血源性交叉传播和患者暴露

condition.en: Expected use of a professional meter with no exposure concern
condition.zh: 专业血糖仪的正常使用，不存在暴露问题

actions.en: Wipe the meter once and return it immediately to routine shared use
actions.zh: 把血糖仪擦拭一次后立即恢复常规共用

actions.en: Notify infection prevention and initiate the facility's trace of all four potentially exposed clients
actions.zh: 通知感染预防部门，并按机构流程追踪全部四名可能暴露的患者

actions.en: Begin empiric post-exposure drug prophylaxis for all four clients before risk evaluation
actions.zh: 在风险评估前立即给全部四名患者开始经验性暴露后药物预防

actions.en: Stop use and secure the meter so it cannot be used again pending evaluation
actions.zh: 停止使用并封存血糖仪，在评估完成前防止再次使用

parameters.en: Exposure evaluation and follow-up are completed and documented for every traced client
parameters.zh: 每名被追踪患者的暴露评估和后续处理均已完成并记录

parameters.en: The staff member who used the meter most often is identified
parameters.zh: 已找出使用该血糖仪次数最多的工作人员

parameters.en: All four clients have glucose values within the reference range
parameters.zh: 四名患者的血糖值都在参考范围内

parameters.en: Corrective action and audit confirm a meter workflow that prevents reuse without cleaning and disinfection
parameters.zh: 纠正措施和审核确认新流程可防止血糖仪未经清洁消毒就再次使用

correct.en: A shared professional meter must be cleaned and disinfected after every use. Failure across four clients creates a potential bloodborne exposure event. The device is stopped and secured, infection prevention initiates tracing, and closure requires both exposed-client evaluation and verified correction of the workflow.
correct.zh: 共用的专业血糖仪必须在每次使用后清洁和消毒。连续在四名患者之间未消毒使用，构成潜在血源性暴露事件。应停止并封存设备，由感染预防部门启动追踪；闭环需要完成暴露患者评估，并确认工作流程已纠正。

byChoice.en: Blood can contaminate shared meters, so missing between-client disinfection creates cross-transmission risk for every client in the sequence.
byChoice.zh: 血液可污染共用血糖仪，因此患者之间未消毒会给整个使用序列中的每名患者带来交叉传播风险。

byChoice.en: Professional-use design permits sharing only when manufacturer-directed cleaning and disinfection occur after every use.
byChoice.zh: 专业用途设计只有在每次使用后按制造商说明清洁和消毒时才允许共用。

byChoice.en: The issue is infection exposure across all four clients, not a dosing error limited to one client.
byChoice.zh: 问题是四名患者的感染暴露，而不是仅影响一名患者的用药错误。

byChoice.en: Securing the device immediately prevents additional unclean use while the event and device are evaluated.
byChoice.zh: 立即封存设备可在评估事件和设备期间防止再次未经清洁使用。

byChoice.en: Infection prevention coordinates the required exposed-client trace and risk-evaluation process.
byChoice.zh: 感染预防部门协调所需的暴露患者追踪和风险评估流程。

byChoice.en: A single wipe does not substitute for validated cleaning and disinfection or address the prior exposures.
byChoice.zh: 简单擦拭一次不能替代经过验证的清洁和消毒，也不能处理既往暴露。

byChoice.en: The scenario requires evaluation and tracing; it does not support automatically giving drug prophylaxis to every client.
byChoice.zh: 该情境要求评估和追踪，并不支持自动给每名患者使用药物预防。

byChoice.en: Every potentially exposed client must be accounted for and receive the facility-directed evaluation and follow-up.
byChoice.zh: 每名可能暴露的患者都必须被纳入，并完成机构规定的评估和随访。

byChoice.en: An audit of the corrected workflow addresses the system cause and helps prevent recurrence.
byChoice.zh: 对纠正后流程进行审核可处理系统原因并帮助防止再次发生。

byChoice.en: Glucose values do not determine whether bloodborne exposure evaluation is complete.
byChoice.zh: 血糖值不能判断血源性暴露评估是否完成。

byChoice.en: Identifying a frequent user does not close client evaluation or repair the unsafe workflow.
byChoice.zh: 找出使用次数最多的人不能完成患者评估，也不能修复不安全流程。

sourceMetadata: CDC, Considerations for Blood Glucose Monitoring and Insulin Administration, Blood Glucose Meters section—shared meters must be cleaned and disinfected after every use, https://www.cdc.gov/injection-safety/hcp/infection-control/

stem.en: A blood-containing specimen tube breaks on the floor. The cleanup plan requires suitable PPE, mechanical collection of glass, sharps disposal, cleaning before disinfection, use of the disinfectant for its stated contact time, and hand hygiene. Classify each action.
stem.zh: 一支含血液的标本管在地面破裂。清理计划要求使用合适的 PPE、用机械方法收集玻璃、放入锐器容器、先清洁后消毒、按消毒剂规定的接触时间使用，并进行手卫生。请对每项行动进行分类。

rows.en: Put on suitable gloves and any additional PPE needed for splash risk.
rows.zh: 戴上合适的手套，并根据飞溅风险使用其他所需 PPE。

rows.en: Pick up the glass fragments with bare hands to clear the walkway quickly.
rows.zh: 为了快速清理通道，徒手捡起玻璃碎片。

rows.en: Use forceps, tongs, or a brush and dustpan to collect the contaminated glass.
rows.zh: 使用镊子、夹钳或刷子和簸箕收集受污染玻璃。

rows.en: Place the contaminated glass fragments in an appropriate sharps container.
rows.zh: 将受污染的玻璃碎片放入合适的锐器容器。

rows.en: Remove visible soil, then apply the approved disinfectant and keep the surface wet for the product's stated contact time.
rows.zh: 先去除可见污物，再使用批准的消毒剂，并让表面在产品规定的接触时间内保持湿润。

rows.en: Perform hand hygiene after removing PPE.
rows.zh: 脱去 PPE 后进行手卫生。

rows.en: Compress a waste bag by hand to make room for more contaminated material.
rows.zh: 用手压实废物袋，以便装入更多受污染物品。

rows.en: Use a vacuum cleaner to collect the contaminated glass fragments.
rows.zh: 使用吸尘器收集受污染的玻璃碎片。

correct.en: Blood-contaminated broken glass is handled with PPE and mechanical tools, never bare hands or a vacuum. Fragments go into a sharps container. The surface is cleaned and then disinfected for the labeled contact time, followed by hand hygiene. Waste bags are not compressed by hand because concealed sharps can cause injury.
correct.zh: 含血液的破碎玻璃应使用 PPE 和机械工具处理，不能徒手或使用吸尘器。碎片应放入锐器容器。地面先清洁，再按标签规定接触时间消毒，最后进行手卫生。不能用手压实废物袋，因为隐藏锐器可能造成损伤。

byChoice.en: PPE reduces skin, mucous-membrane, and splash exposure during cleanup.
byChoice.zh: PPE 可减少清理过程中的皮肤、黏膜和飞溅暴露。

byChoice.en: Bare-hand pickup creates a percutaneous injury and blood-exposure risk.
byChoice.zh: 徒手捡拾会造成经皮损伤和血液暴露风险。

byChoice.en: Mechanical means keep hands away from contaminated sharp edges.
byChoice.zh: 机械工具可使手远离受污染的锋利边缘。

byChoice.en: Contaminated glass is a sharp and belongs in a puncture-resistant sharps container.
byChoice.zh: 受污染玻璃属于锐器，应放入防穿刺锐器容器。

byChoice.en: Cleaning removes soil that can interfere with disinfection, and the stated contact time is needed for the product to work as intended.
byChoice.zh: 清洁可去除妨碍消毒的污物，而规定接触时间是消毒剂按预期发挥作用所必需的。

byChoice.en: Hand hygiene is required after glove and PPE removal because contamination can occur during removal.
byChoice.zh: 脱去手套和 PPE 时可能发生污染，因此之后必须进行手卫生。

byChoice.en: Hand-compressing waste can expose the worker to concealed glass or other sharps.
byChoice.zh: 用手压实废物可能使工作人员接触隐藏的玻璃或其他锐器。

byChoice.en: A vacuum is not appropriate for contaminated broken glass and can spread contamination or expose equipment and staff.
byChoice.zh: 吸尘器不适合清理受污染的碎玻璃，可能扩散污染或使设备和人员暴露。

sourceMetadata: OSHA, Enforcement Procedures for the Occupational Exposure to Bloodborne Pathogens, CPL 2-2.44D, contaminated broken glass—mechanical handling, sharps-container disposal, and no vacuum, https://www.osha.gov/enforcement/directives/cpl-2-244d; CDC, Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices, Environmental Cleaning and Disinfection—follow manufacturer instructions including contact time, https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/core-practices/index.html

stem.en: A client with a high-output ileostomy has pH 7.29, PaCO2 29 mm Hg, HCO3 14 mEq/L, sodium 138 mEq/L, and chloride 112 mEq/L. Use: anion gap = Na − (Cl + HCO3); normal anion gap = 8–12 mEq/L; expected PaCO2 = 1.5(HCO3) + 8 ± 2 mm Hg.
stem.zh: 一名高输出回肠造口患者的结果为：pH 7.29、PaCO2 29 mm Hg、HCO3 14 mEq/L、钠 138 mEq/L、氯 112 mEq/L。使用以下公式：阴离子间隙 = Na −（Cl + HCO3）；正常阴离子间隙 = 8–12 mEq/L；预期 PaCO2 = 1.5(HCO3) + 8 ± 2 mm Hg。

clozeStem.en: These results show {{q16_d1}} caused by {{q16_d2}}, with {{q16_d3}}.
clozeStem.zh: 这些结果显示{{q16_d1}}，由{{q16_d2}}引起，并伴有{{q16_d3}}。

options.en: high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis
options.zh: 高阴离子间隙代谢性酸中毒

options.en: normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis
options.zh: 正常阴离子间隙代谢性酸中毒

options.en: primary respiratory alkalosis
options.zh: 原发性呼吸性碱中毒

options.en: intestinal bicarbonate loss from the ileostomy
options.zh: 回肠造口导致的肠道碳酸氢盐丢失

options.en: lactic acid accumulation from shock
options.zh: 休克导致的乳酸堆积

options.en: carbon dioxide retention from hypoventilation
options.zh: 低通气导致的二氧化碳潴留

options.en: appropriate respiratory compensation
options.zh: 适当的呼吸性代偿

options.en: a superimposed respiratory alkalosis
options.zh: 合并呼吸性碱中毒

options.en: a superimposed respiratory acidosis
options.zh: 合并呼吸性酸中毒

correct.en: The pH is acidemic and HCO3 is low, so the primary process is metabolic acidosis. The anion gap is 138 − (112 + 14) = 12 mEq/L, which is normal. A high-output ileostomy causes gastrointestinal bicarbonate loss. Expected PaCO2 is 1.5(14) + 8 = 29 ± 2 mm Hg; the measured 29 mm Hg shows appropriate respiratory compensation.
correct.zh: pH 表示酸血症，HCO3 降低，因此原发过程是代谢性酸中毒。阴离子间隙为 138 −（112 + 14）= 12 mEq/L，属于正常范围。高输出回肠造口可导致胃肠道碳酸氢盐丢失。预期 PaCO2 为 1.5(14) + 8 = 29 ± 2 mm Hg；实测 29 mm Hg，说明呼吸性代偿适当。

byChoice.en: The correct choice is normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis: acidemia plus low HCO3 establishes metabolic acidosis, and the calculated gap is 12. A gap of 12 is not high, and low HCO3 is not explained by isolated primary respiratory alkalosis.
byChoice.zh: 正确选择是正常阴离子间隙代谢性酸中毒：酸血症加低 HCO3 确立代谢性酸中毒，计算间隙为 12。12 不属于高间隙，单纯原发性呼吸性碱中毒也不能解释该低 HCO3 情境。

byChoice.en: The correct cause is intestinal bicarbonate loss from the high-output ileostomy. Lactic acidosis usually raises the anion gap, and carbon dioxide retention would raise rather than lower PaCO2.
byChoice.zh: 正确原因是高输出回肠造口导致的肠道碳酸氢盐丢失。乳酸性酸中毒通常会升高阴离子间隙，而二氧化碳潴留会使 PaCO2 升高而不是降低。

byChoice.en: The correct interpretation is appropriate compensation because measured PaCO2 equals the center of the expected 27–31 mm Hg range. A value above the range would suggest respiratory acidosis; a value below it would suggest respiratory alkalosis.
byChoice.zh: 正确解释是适当代偿，因为实测 PaCO2 等于预期 27–31 mm Hg 范围的中心值。高于该范围提示合并呼吸性酸中毒，低于该范围提示合并呼吸性碱中毒。

sourceMetadata: Merck Manual Professional Edition, Metabolic Acidosis, Causes of Metabolic Acidosis table (normal-gap gastrointestinal bicarbonate loss including ileostomy) and Diagnosis of Metabolic Acidosis (anion-gap evaluation and Winter's formula), https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/nephrology/acid-base-regulation-and-disorders/metabolic-acidosis

stem.en: A capable inpatient tells the nurse, “My close friend is the person I want to visit and support me.” Staff plan to exclude the friend solely because the friend is not legally related to the client. No safety restriction is currently in effect.
stem.zh: 一名具有决定能力的住院患者告诉护士：“我希望我的亲密朋友来探视并支持我。”工作人员仅因该朋友与患者没有法律亲属关系而计划拒绝其探视。目前没有实施任何安全限制。

options.en: honor the client’s designation of the friend as a visitor
options.zh: 尊重患者指定该朋友为探视者的决定

options.en: require the visitor to prove a legal family relationship
options.zh: 要求探视者证明其与患者存在法律亲属关系

options.en: allow the client’s relatives to choose all permitted visitors
options.zh: 由患者亲属决定所有获准探视者

options.en: the friend does not hold healthcare power of attorney
options.zh: 该朋友没有医疗授权委托书

options.en: a staff member is uncomfortable with nonrelative visitors
options.zh: 工作人员对非亲属探视者感到不自在

options.en: a clinically necessary or otherwise reasonable restriction applies consistently and is explained
options.zh: 存在临床必要或其他合理限制，且该限制被一致执行并得到说明

correct.en: A capable client may designate a friend as a visitor. The hospital may apply clinically necessary or otherwise reasonable visitation limits, but it may not exclude the friend merely because the friend is not legally related to the client. Any applicable restriction should be consistently implemented and explained.
correct.zh: 具有决定能力的患者可以指定朋友为探视者。医院可以实施临床必要或其他合理的探视限制，但不能仅因该朋友不是法律亲属而拒绝探视。任何适用限制都应一致执行并予以说明。

byChoice.en: Honor the client’s stated visitor preference; legal kinship and healthcare power of attorney are not prerequisites for ordinary visitation.
byChoice.zh: 应尊重患者表达的探视偏好；法律亲属关系和医疗授权委托书都不是普通探视的前提。

byChoice.en: Visitation is not unlimited. A clinically necessary or otherwise reasonable restriction may apply when it is consistently implemented and the reason is explained; staff discomfort alone is not a valid basis.
byChoice.zh: 探视权并非无限制。若限制具有临床必要性或其他合理依据、被一致执行且说明理由，则可以适用；仅有工作人员的不适感不是有效依据。

sourceMetadata: CMS State Operations Manual, Appendix A, 42 CFR 482.13(h), Tags A-0215–A-0217, including patient-designated visitors, clinically necessary or reasonable restrictions, nondiscrimination, and equal visitation privileges: https://www.cms.gov/Regulations-and-Guidance/Guidance/Transmittals/downloads/R75SOMA.pdf

stem.en: A client with dysarthria is alert and has decision-making capacity. The client uses a speech-generating device and communicates slowly. For each proposed staff behavior, indicate whether it supports the client’s communication rights and autonomy.
stem.zh: 一名构音障碍患者意识清醒并具有决定能力。患者使用语音生成设备，沟通速度较慢。请判断每项工作人员行为是否支持患者的沟通权利和自主性。

rows.en: Ask the client which communication method works best.
rows.zh: 询问患者哪种沟通方式最有效。

rows.en: Provide the speech-generating device and allow the client to use it.
rows.zh: 提供语音生成设备并允许患者使用。

rows.en: Allow enough time for the client to complete each response.
rows.zh: 给予患者足够时间完成每次回答。

rows.en: Address questions directly to the client.
rows.zh: 直接向患者提问。

rows.en: Respectfully ask the client to repeat or clarify an unclear word.
rows.zh: 对不清楚的词语，礼貌地请患者重复或澄清。

rows.en: Finish the client’s sentences to keep the interview moving.
rows.zh: 为了加快访谈进度，替患者说完句子。

rows.en: Direct all questions to the companion because communication is faster.
rows.zh: 因为沟通更快，把所有问题都问陪同者。

rows.en: Treat impaired speech as evidence that the client cannot make decisions.
rows.zh: 把言语受损视为患者不能作出决定的证据。

correct.en: Effective communication preserves the client’s own voice: use the client’s preferred method, provide the auxiliary aid, allow time, address the client directly, and clarify respectfully. Dysarthria does not establish impaired cognition or decision-making capacity.
correct.zh: 有效沟通应保留患者本人的声音：采用患者偏好的方式、提供辅助设备、给予时间、直接与患者交流，并以尊重的方式澄清。构音障碍并不等于认知或决定能力受损。

byChoice.en: The person with the disability is the best starting point for identifying an effective communication method.
byChoice.zh: 残障人士本人是确定有效沟通方式的最佳起点。

byChoice.en: Providing and allowing use of the client’s usual auxiliary aid supports effective communication.
byChoice.zh: 提供并允许使用患者平时使用的辅助设备，有助于有效沟通。

byChoice.en: Allowing additional response time accommodates a speech disability without taking over the conversation.
byChoice.zh: 给予额外回答时间可以适应言语障碍，同时不会代替患者沟通。

byChoice.en: The client retains decision-making authority and should be addressed directly.
byChoice.zh: 患者仍保有决定权，应直接与患者交流。

byChoice.en: Respectful clarification improves accuracy while preserving the client’s control of the message.
byChoice.zh: 礼貌澄清可提高准确性，同时保留患者对信息的控制。

byChoice.en: Finishing sentences can distort the message and remove the client’s opportunity to speak for themself.
byChoice.zh: 替患者说完句子可能歪曲信息，也会剥夺患者自行表达的机会。

byChoice.en: A companion may assist when the client wants, but should not replace direct communication with a capable client.
byChoice.zh: 在患者愿意时陪同者可以协助，但不能取代与有决定能力患者的直接沟通。

byChoice.en: Speech impairment alone does not demonstrate impaired cognition or decision-making capacity.
byChoice.zh: 言语受损本身不能证明认知或决定能力受损。

sourceMetadata: U.S. Department of Justice, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, sections on auxiliary aids for speech disabilities, considering the person’s normal method of communication, allowing more time, and respectfully clarifying unclear speech: https://www.ada.gov/resources/effective-communication/

stem.en: Day and night shifts repeatedly accuse each other of failing to restock a time-critical airway cart. No client is currently deteriorating. An objective audit shows that responsibility changes at 1900, but the handoff checklist names no owner and includes no verification step. Complete the bowtie.
stem.zh: 日班和夜班反复互相指责未补充需要及时备齐的气道车。目前没有患者病情恶化。客观审计显示，责任在1900交接，但交接清单没有指定负责人，也没有核实步骤。完成蝴蝶结题。

condition.en: Role and process ambiguity at shift handoff
condition.zh: 交班时的角色与流程不明确

condition.en: A confirmed hospital-wide supply shortage
condition.zh: 已证实的全院物资短缺

condition.en: A knowledge deficit about airway equipment
condition.zh: 对气道设备的知识不足

condition.en: An active airway emergency
condition.zh: 正在发生的气道急症

actions.en: Send separate warning emails to each shift
actions.zh: 分别向每个班次发送警告邮件

actions.en: Hold a joint day-night huddle using the audit facts
actions.zh: 根据审计事实召开日夜班联合短会

actions.en: Revise the handoff to name an owner and require closed-loop verification
actions.zh: 修改交接流程，指定负责人并要求闭环核实

actions.en: Discipline the most recent nurse who signed the checklist
actions.zh: 处分最近在清单上签字的护士

actions.en: Wait for another omission before changing the process
actions.zh: 等再次发生遗漏后再改变流程

parameters.en: Completion of the new owner-and-verification handoff check
parameters.zh: 新的负责人及核实交接检查完成率

parameters.en: Total unit overtime unrelated to restocking
parameters.zh: 与补货无关的科室总加班时间

parameters.en: Recurrence of airway-cart stock omissions
parameters.zh: 气道车物资遗漏是否再次发生

parameters.en: Number of informal complaints about the other shift
parameters.zh: 对另一班次的非正式抱怨次数

parameters.en: How quickly the huddle ends
parameters.zh: 短会结束得多快

correct.en: The audit identifies a recurring ownership and verification gap, not an individual character flaw. A joint huddle creates a shared plan; naming the owner and requiring closed-loop verification makes the handoff accountable. Monitor whether the new check occurs and whether omissions recur.
correct.zh: 审计发现的是反复出现的责任归属和核实缺口，而不是个人品格问题。联合短会可形成共同计划；指定负责人并要求闭环核实，可使交接具有明确责任。应监测新检查是否完成以及遗漏是否再次发生。

byChoice.en: The handoff lacks both a named owner and a verification step, which sustains role and process ambiguity.
byChoice.zh: 交接同时缺少指定负责人和核实步骤，导致角色与流程持续不明确。

byChoice.en: The audit does not show that staff lack knowledge of the cart contents.
byChoice.zh: 审计没有显示工作人员不了解气道车内容。

byChoice.en: The problem is assignment and verification, not a confirmed supply shortage.
byChoice.zh: 问题在于责任分配和核实，而不是已证实的物资短缺。

byChoice.en: The stem explicitly states that no client is currently deteriorating.
byChoice.zh: 题干明确说明目前没有患者病情恶化。

byChoice.en: A joint huddle lets both shifts review objective facts and agree on the updated plan.
byChoice.zh: 联合短会可让两个班次根据客观事实达成更新后的共同计划。

byChoice.en: A named owner plus read-back or confirmation closes the communication loop.
byChoice.zh: 指定负责人并进行复述或确认可完成沟通闭环。

byChoice.en: Separate warnings preserve the shift-versus-shift framing rather than create a shared process.
byChoice.zh: 分别警告会保留班次对立，而不是建立共同流程。

byChoice.en: Punishing the last signer does not correct the checklist’s structural ambiguity.
byChoice.zh: 处分最后签字者不能纠正清单的结构性不明确。

byChoice.en: Waiting exposes the unit to another preventable omission.
byChoice.zh: 等待会使科室再次面临可预防的遗漏。

byChoice.en: This process measure shows whether the revised handoff is actually used.
byChoice.zh: 该流程指标显示修改后的交接是否真正执行。

byChoice.en: Recurrence is the safety outcome the process change is intended to reduce.
byChoice.zh: 再次发生遗漏是该流程改变要减少的安全结果。

byChoice.en: Informal complaint counts do not establish cart reliability.
byChoice.zh: 非正式抱怨次数不能证明气道车是否可靠备齐。

byChoice.en: A shorter huddle is not evidence that the handoff is safer.
byChoice.zh: 短会更快结束并不证明交接更安全。

byChoice.en: Unrelated overtime does not evaluate the targeted intervention.
byChoice.zh: 无关的加班时间不能评价这一针对性干预。

sourceMetadata: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS, Huddle tool (adjusting and communicating the plan) and Closed-Loop Communication tool (message, receiver confirmation, sender verification): https://www.ahrq.gov/teamstepps-program/curriculum/team/tools/huddle.html ; https://www.ahrq.gov/teamstepps-program/curriculum/communication/tools/loop.html

stem.en: A client experiencing intimate-partner stalking asks the clinic to send appointment reminders only to a new email address and not to the home telephone or mailing address.
stem.zh: 一名遭受亲密伴侣跟踪的患者要求诊所只把预约提醒发送到新的电子邮箱，不要发送到家庭电话或邮寄地址。

clozeStem.en: This is a request for {{q05_request}}; the nurse should {{q05_action}}.

options.en: amendment of a disputed diagnosis
options.zh: 修改有争议的诊断

options.en: confidential communications by an alternative means or location
options.zh: 通过替代方式或地点进行保密通信

options.en: immediate access to the complete medical record
options.zh: 立即访问完整医疗记录

options.en: continue all existing reminder channels until the client obtains a court order
options.zh: 在患者取得法院命令前继续使用所有现有提醒渠道

options.en: route and document the request through the covered entity’s confidential-communications process and stop using the unsafe channels as directed
options.zh: 按照受监管实体的保密通信流程转交并记录该请求，并按要求停止使用不安全渠道

options.en: require the client to prove the stalking before changing contact methods
options.zh: 要求患者证明遭跟踪后才改变联系方式

correct.en: HIPAA permits an individual to request communications by an alternative means or at an alternative location. The clinic should use its established process to record and implement the reasonable request rather than continue channels the client has identified as unsafe.
correct.zh: HIPAA允许个人请求通过替代方式或替代地点进行通信。诊所应使用既定流程记录并实施合理请求，而不是继续使用患者已指出不安全的渠道。

byChoice.en: The client is changing how and where protected health information is communicated, not seeking access or an amendment.
byChoice.zh: 患者是在改变受保护健康信息的通信方式和地点，而不是申请查阅或修改记录。

byChoice.en: The request should be routed through the covered entity’s process and implemented when reasonable; proof of the underlying danger is not the nursing decision tested.
byChoice.zh: 应通过受监管实体的流程处理，并在合理时实施；本题不要求护士判断患者是否证明了危险。

sourceMetadata: 45 CFR 164.522(b), Confidential communications requirements, including requests for communications by alternative means or at alternative locations and covered-entity processes: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.522

stem.en: A client will leave today on outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT). Infusion supplies will arrive before the first home dose. The prescribed plan is a complete blood count and metabolic panel every Monday and Thursday, but no recipient is named for the results. No clinician or team has accepted responsibility for the OPAT course, and follow-up is not booked. Complete the bowtie.
stem.zh: 一名患者今天将带院外静脉抗菌治疗（OPAT）出院。输注用品将在首次居家用药前送达。医嘱监测计划为每周一和周四进行全血细胞计数和代谢检查，但没有指定结果接收者。没有临床医生或团队接受OPAT疗程责任，随访也未预约。完成蝴蝶结题。

condition.en: Intentional refusal of all treatment
condition.zh: 故意拒绝所有治疗

condition.en: Delayed infusion-supply delivery
condition.zh: 输注用品延迟送达

condition.en: Unsafe, unowned OPAT transition
condition.zh: 不安全且无人负责的OPAT过渡

condition.en: Confirmed immediate antimicrobial allergy
condition.zh: 已确认的即刻抗菌药过敏

actions.en: Confirm the OPAT or infectious-diseases clinician/team that accepts responsibility for the course
actions.zh: 确认接受疗程责任的OPAT或感染病临床医生/团队

actions.en: Replace the prescribed schedule with daily laboratory testing
actions.zh: 把医嘱计划改成每日化验

actions.en: Make the client solely responsible for finding a clinician after discharge
actions.zh: 让患者独自负责出院后寻找临床医生

actions.en: Wait for an abnormal result before assigning responsibility
actions.zh: 等出现异常结果后再指定责任人

actions.en: Transmit the antimicrobial regimen and the prescribed Monday/Thursday monitoring plan to that responsible clinician/team
actions.zh: 把抗菌方案和每周一/周四监测计划传递给该负责临床医生/团队

actions.en: Discharge because supply delivery alone makes the transition complete
actions.zh: 仅因用品已安排送达就出院

parameters.en: Attendance at follow-up and documented clinical assessment of the OPAT course
parameters.zh: 按时随访并记录对OPAT疗程的临床评估

parameters.en: Receipt and documented review of the scheduled laboratory results
parameters.zh: 按计划化验结果的接收和有记录的审阅

parameters.en: Number of supply boxes delivered
parameters.zh: 送达的用品箱数量

parameters.en: Number of calls the client makes to locate a clinician
parameters.zh: 患者为寻找临床医生拨打电话的次数

parameters.en: Completion of unprescribed daily laboratory tests
parameters.zh: 完成未开具的每日化验

correct.en: Supply delivery does not make OPAT safe when clinical ownership, result routing, and follow-up are absent. Before discharge, a responsible OPAT/ID clinician or team must accept oversight and receive the regimen and prescribed monitoring plan. The transition is evaluated by confirming that scheduled results are received and reviewed and that clinical follow-up occurs.
correct.zh: 仅有用品送达并不能在缺少临床责任、结果转交和随访时保证OPAT安全。出院前，必须由负责的OPAT/感染病临床医生或团队接受监督责任，并接收抗菌方案和医嘱监测计划。应通过确认计划结果被接收和审阅，以及临床随访确实发生来评价过渡。

byChoice.en: No clinician owns the course, no one is named to receive results, and follow-up is unbooked.
byChoice.zh: 没有临床医生负责疗程、没有指定结果接收者，且随访未预约。

byChoice.en: The stem confirms timely supply delivery.
byChoice.zh: 题干确认用品会及时送达。

byChoice.en: No allergy findings are provided.
byChoice.zh: 题干未提供过敏表现。

byChoice.en: The client has not refused therapy.
byChoice.zh: 患者并未拒绝治疗。

byChoice.en: Named clinical ownership is required for ongoing OPAT oversight and response to problems.
byChoice.zh: 持续OPAT监督和问题处理需要明确的临床责任人。

byChoice.en: The responsible team must receive the regimen and the exact prescribed monitoring plan.
byChoice.zh: 负责团队必须接收抗菌方案和准确的医嘱监测计划。

byChoice.en: The producer should not invent a universal frequency or override the prescribed plan.
byChoice.zh: 不应臆造统一频率或更改医嘱计划。

byChoice.en: Logistics are necessary but do not replace clinical oversight.
byChoice.zh: 物流安排是必要的，但不能替代临床监督。

byChoice.en: The transition team must establish responsibility rather than shift the coordination burden to the client.
byChoice.zh: 过渡团队必须建立责任机制，而不是把协调负担转给患者。

byChoice.en: Responsibility must be established before a result requires action.
byChoice.zh: 必须在结果需要处理之前建立责任。

byChoice.en: Result receipt and review show that the monitoring loop is functioning.
byChoice.zh: 结果被接收和审阅表明监测闭环正在运行。

byChoice.en: Clinical follow-up evaluates tolerance, response, complications, and continuation of the plan.
byChoice.zh: 临床随访可评价耐受性、疗效、并发症及计划延续。

byChoice.en: Box counts do not show whether clinical monitoring occurs.
byChoice.zh: 用品箱数量不能证明临床监测是否发生。

byChoice.en: Requiring the client to search for oversight indicates a failed transition, not a successful outcome.
byChoice.zh: 让患者自行寻找监督者表明过渡失败，而不是成功结果。

byChoice.en: Unprescribed testing is not the stated monitoring outcome.
byChoice.zh: 未开具的检查不是题干规定的监测结果。

sourceMetadata: IDSA, Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Outpatient Parenteral Antimicrobial Therapy, Recommendations 14 and 16 and discussion of responsible oversight and availability of laboratory results to the responsible team: https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/outpatient-parenteral-antimicrobial-therapy/

stem.en: An adult with uncomplicated mild traumatic brain injury has completed an emergency evaluation that supports discharge. The draft discharge record contains only: “Use acetaminophen as directed and rest tonight.” Highlight the additional elements that should be added before discharge.
stem.zh: 一名无并发症的轻度创伤性脑损伤成人已完成急诊评估，评估支持出院。出院记录草稿仅写有：“按说明使用对乙酰氨基酚，今晚休息。”请标出出院前应补充的内容。

segments.en: Provide verbal and written instructions about delayed danger signs and when to seek emergency care.
segments.zh: 口头并书面说明延迟出现的危险征象以及何时寻求急救。

segments.en: With the client’s agreement, tell a chosen family member or friend what symptoms to watch for.
segments.zh: 经患者同意，告知其选择的家人或朋友需要观察哪些症状。

segments.en: Arrange or specify follow-up with the regular clinician within a few days.
segments.zh: 安排或明确在数日内与常规临床医生随访。

segments.en: Give individualized written guidance for return to work, driving, and other activities.
segments.zh: 提供关于恢复工作、驾驶和其他活动的个体化书面指导。

segments.en: Schedule routine repeat head CT tomorrow despite the discharge-supporting evaluation.
segments.zh: 尽管评估支持出院，仍常规安排明日重复头部CT。

segments.en: Require overnight hospital admission solely because mild TBI was diagnosed.
segments.zh: 仅因诊断为轻度脑损伤而要求住院过夜。

segments.en: Tell the client to resume all activities whenever the client feels ready, without written limits.
segments.zh: 只告诉患者感觉可以时恢复所有活动，不提供书面限制。

correct.en: Safe mild-TBI discharge includes verbal and written danger-sign education, involvement of a chosen support person, follow-up within the stated timeframe, and individualized written return-to-activity guidance. Routine repeat imaging or admission is not required when the completed evaluation supports discharge.
correct.zh: 安全的轻度脑损伤出院包括口头和书面危险征象教育、让患者选择的支持者了解观察要点、在规定时间内随访，以及个体化书面活动恢复指导。当完成的评估支持出院时，不需要常规重复影像或住院。

byChoice.en: Delayed deterioration is uncommon but requires clear verbal and written emergency instructions.
byChoice.zh: 延迟恶化虽少见，但需要清楚的口头和书面急救说明。

byChoice.en: A chosen support person may notice concerning changes before the client does.
byChoice.zh: 患者选择的支持者可能比患者本人更早发现异常变化。

byChoice.en: Follow-up within a few days supports reassessment and recovery planning.
byChoice.zh: 数日内随访有助于重新评估和恢复计划。

byChoice.en: Return to work, driving, and activity should be individualized and written.
byChoice.zh: 恢复工作、驾驶和活动的指导应个体化并以书面形式提供。

byChoice.en: Routine repeat imaging is not indicated solely because the client has mild TBI when the evaluation supports discharge.
byChoice.zh: 当评估支持出院时，不能仅因轻度脑损伤就常规重复影像。

byChoice.en: Routine admission is not required without another clinical indication.
byChoice.zh: 没有其他临床指征时不需要常规住院。

byChoice.en: Unqualified verbal advice does not provide individualized, reviewable activity guidance.
byChoice.zh: 笼统的口头建议不能提供个体化、可复查的活动指导。

sourceMetadata: CDC, Mild Traumatic Brain Injury and Concussion: Information for Adults—Discharge Instructions, danger signs, family/friend observation, follow-up, and written return-to-activity guidance: https://www.cdc.gov/traumatic-brain-injury/media/pdfs/TBI_Patient_Instructions-a.pdf ; CDC Checklist to Assess for and Manage Adult mTBI, discharge education, follow-up within a few days, and no routine repeat imaging/admission when criteria support discharge: https://www.cdc.gov/traumaticbraininjury/pdf/checklist_adult_mTBI-508.pdf

stem.en: A spouse is listed as the sole helper for a newly dependent stroke client. During discharge planning, the spouse says, “The therapist needed two people for the transfer. I cannot do that alone, and I am afraid I will drop my partner.” Complete the bowtie.
stem.zh: 一名配偶被列为新近依赖他人照护的脑卒中患者的唯一帮助者。在出院计划中，配偶说：“治疗师转移患者时需要两个人。我一个人做不到，也担心会把伴侣摔下来。”完成蝴蝶结题。

condition.en: The spouse is intentionally delaying discharge
condition.zh: 配偶故意拖延出院

condition.en: The client has no rehabilitation needs
condition.zh: 患者没有康复需求

condition.en: The discharge plan exceeds the willing caregiver’s physical capacity
condition.zh: 出院计划超出愿意照护者的身体能力

condition.en: The caregiver is refusing all participation
condition.zh: 照护者拒绝所有参与

actions.en: Tell the spouse that family members are expected to manage after discharge
actions.zh: 告诉配偶家属理应在出院后自行处理

actions.en: Require repeated solo practice until the spouse agrees
actions.zh: 要求配偶反复单人练习直到同意

actions.en: Revise equipment, personnel, and home-support arrangements to match the assessed need
actions.zh: 根据评估需求修改设备、人员和居家支持安排

actions.en: Document the spouse as nonadherent
actions.zh: 把配偶记录为不依从

actions.en: Ask therapy to reassess the transfer method and required level of assistance
actions.zh: 请治疗团队重新评估转移方式和所需协助程度

parameters.en: Discharge occurs on the original date regardless of support
parameters.zh: 无论支持是否到位都按原日期出院

parameters.en: The spouse signs a general caregiver form
parameters.zh: 配偶签署一般照护者表格

parameters.en: The actual home-support schedule and responsible helpers are confirmed
parameters.zh: 确认实际居家支持时间表和负责帮助者

parameters.en: A safe transfer plan is demonstrated using the actual recommended assistance and equipment
parameters.zh: 使用实际推荐的协助和设备演示安全转移计划

parameters.en: The spouse says, “I will try harder.”
parameters.zh: 配偶说：“我会更努力。”

correct.en: The spouse is willing but cannot safely provide the two-person transfer alone. The team should reassess the transfer and revise equipment, staffing, or home support. Readiness requires a demonstrated safe method and confirmation that the needed helpers will actually be present.
correct.zh: 配偶愿意照护，但无法独自安全完成需要两人的转移。团队应重新评估转移，并修改设备、人员或居家支持安排。只有安全方法得到演示且所需帮助者确实能够到场，才算准备完成。

byChoice.en: The caregiver states a concrete physical limit and safety concern.
byChoice.zh: 照护者说明了具体身体限制和安全担忧。

byChoice.en: The spouse is not refusing; the spouse is identifying an unsafe mismatch.
byChoice.zh: 配偶不是拒绝，而是在指出不安全的不匹配。

byChoice.en: A two-person transfer indicates substantial assistance needs.
byChoice.zh: 需要两人转移表明患者有明显协助需求。

byChoice.en: No evidence suggests intentional delay.
byChoice.zh: 没有证据表明故意拖延。

byChoice.en: Therapy can determine whether technique, equipment, or assistance level should change.
byChoice.zh: 治疗团队可判断技术、设备或协助程度是否需要改变。

byChoice.en: The plan must match the caregiver’s actual capacity and available support.
byChoice.zh: 计划必须符合照护者实际能力和可用支持。

byChoice.en: Family relationship does not make an unsafe task feasible.
byChoice.zh: 家属身份不会使不安全的任务变得可行。

byChoice.en: Calling the spouse nonadherent mischaracterizes a valid capacity concern.
byChoice.zh: 把配偶称为不依从会错误描述其合理的能力担忧。

byChoice.en: Practice cannot substitute for a second person when two-person assistance remains necessary.
byChoice.zh: 当仍需两人协助时，练习不能替代第二名帮助者。

byChoice.en: Demonstration with the actual plan verifies physical safety.
byChoice.zh: 使用实际计划进行演示可验证身体安全。

byChoice.en: A confirmed schedule verifies that required help will be available when needed.
byChoice.zh: 确认时间表可验证所需帮助会在需要时到位。

byChoice.en: A statement of effort does not prove feasibility.
byChoice.zh: 表达努力意愿不能证明计划可行。

byChoice.en: The date is not a safety outcome.
byChoice.zh: 出院日期本身不是安全结果。

byChoice.en: A signature does not demonstrate capacity or available help.
byChoice.zh: 签名不能证明能力或可用帮助。

sourceMetadata: CMS State Operations Manual, Appendix PP, §483.21(c)(1)(iv) and F660/F661 discharge-planning guidance requiring consideration of caregiver/support-person availability, capacity, and capability: https://www.cms.gov/Regulations-and-Guidance/Guidance/Manuals/downloads/som107ap_pp_guidelines_ltcf.pdf ; AHRQ IDEAL Discharge Planning, include and listen to patients/families and assess understanding with teach-back: https://www.ahrq.gov/patient-safety/patients-families/engagingfamilies/strategy4/index.html

stem.en: A client has prolonged nasogastric suction. Results are pH 7.51, PaCO2 48 mm Hg, HCO3 37 mEq/L, and chloride 88 mEq/L. The client has no chronic lung disease. For this item, use 40 mm Hg as the reference PaCO2. For metabolic alkalosis, expected PaCO2 rises about 0.6–0.75 mm Hg for each 1 mEq/L rise in HCO3 above 24 mEq/L and generally does not exceed 55 mm Hg from compensation alone.
stem.zh: 一名患者长期接受鼻胃管吸引。检查结果：pH 7.51、PaCO2 48 mm Hg、HCO3 37 mEq/L、氯 88 mEq/L。患者无慢性肺病。本题以40 mm Hg作为PaCO2参考值。代谢性碱中毒时，HCO3每高于24 mEq/L 1 mEq/L，预计PaCO2约升高0.6–0.75 mm Hg；仅由代偿引起的PaCO2通常不超过55 mm Hg。

options.en: primary respiratory acidosis from chronic lung disease
options.zh: 慢性肺病导致的原发性呼吸性酸中毒

options.en: high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis
options.zh: 高阴离子间隙代谢性酸中毒

options.en: chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis from gastric acid and chloride loss
options.zh: 因胃酸和氯丢失导致的氯反应性代谢性碱中毒

options.en: appropriate respiratory compensation
options.zh: 适当的呼吸性代偿

options.en: no respiratory compensation
options.zh: 无呼吸性代偿

options.en: a superimposed primary respiratory acidosis
options.zh: 叠加的原发性呼吸性酸中毒

correct.en: Alkalemia with elevated HCO3 identifies metabolic alkalosis. Prolonged gastric suction removes hydrogen and chloride, producing a chloride-responsive pattern. HCO3 is 13 mEq/L above 24, so expected PaCO2 is approximately 40 + (13 × 0.6–0.75), or about 48–50 mm Hg. The measured PaCO2 of 48 mm Hg is appropriate compensation.
correct.zh: 碱血症伴HCO3升高提示代谢性碱中毒。长期胃内容物吸引会丢失氢离子和氯，形成氯反应性模式。HCO3比24高13 mEq/L，因此预计PaCO2约为40 +（13 × 0.6–0.75），即约48–50 mm Hg。实测PaCO2为48 mm Hg，符合适当代偿。

byChoice.en: The pH and bicarbonate establish metabolic alkalosis, and gastric suction plus low chloride identify chloride loss as the cause.
byChoice.zh: pH和碳酸氢盐确定代谢性碱中毒，胃吸引和低氯提示氯丢失是原因。

byChoice.en: The measured PaCO2 falls within the expected compensatory range; it does not require a second primary respiratory disorder.
byChoice.zh: 实测PaCO2位于预计代偿范围内，不需要另加原发性呼吸障碍解释。

sourceMetadata: Merck Manual Professional, Metabolic Alkalosis, causes including nasogastric suction and chloride-responsive alkalosis: https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/nephrology/acid-base-regulation-and-disorders/metabolic-alkalosis ; Merck Manual table, Primary Changes and Compensations in Simple Acid-Base Disorders, expected PaCO2 rise of 0.6–0.75 mm Hg per 1 mEq/L HCO3 increase and usual maximum 55 mm Hg: https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/multimedia/table/primary-changes-and-compensations-in-simple-acid-base-disorders

stem.en: Minutes after a peripheral nerve block, a client reports metallic taste and tinnitus, becomes agitated, has a seizure, and then develops hypotension with a wide-complex dysrhythmia. The facility LAST protocol directs staff to stop local-anesthetic administration, activate the LAST rescue pathway, support the airway, treat the seizure, and administer 20% lipid emulsion according to the protocol. Complete the bowtie.
stem.zh: 周围神经阻滞后数分钟，患者报告金属味和耳鸣，随后躁动、癫痫发作，并出现低血压和宽QRS心律失常。机构的LAST流程要求停止局麻药给药、启动LAST救援流程、支持气道、处理癫痫，并按流程给予20%脂肪乳。完成蝴蝶结题。

condition.en: Malignant hyperthermia
condition.zh: 恶性高热

condition.en: Expected peripheral nerve-block effect
condition.zh: 周围神经阻滞的预期作用

condition.en: Local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST)
condition.zh: 局部麻醉药全身毒性（LAST）

condition.en: Isolated anaphylaxis
condition.zh: 单纯过敏性休克

actions.en: Ambulate the client to improve circulation
actions.zh: 让患者下床活动以改善循环

actions.en: Stop local-anesthetic administration and activate the LAST rescue pathway
actions.zh: 停止局麻药给药并启动LAST救援流程

actions.en: Provide airway/seizure support and begin 20% lipid emulsion per the supplied protocol
actions.zh: 提供气道和癫痫支持，并按既定流程开始20%脂肪乳

actions.en: Administer another dose of local anesthetic to complete the block
actions.zh: 再给予一剂局麻药以完成阻滞

actions.en: Use routine standard-ACLS medication doses without modification
actions.zh: 不作调整地使用常规标准ACLS药物剂量

actions.en: Observe for 30 minutes before calling for help
actions.zh: 观察30分钟后再呼救

parameters.en: Cardiac rhythm and hemodynamic stability
parameters.zh: 心律和血流动力学稳定性

parameters.en: Whether the client still notices the lipid emulsion taste
parameters.zh: 患者是否仍能尝到脂肪乳味道

parameters.en: Persistence of numbness in the blocked limb
parameters.zh: 阻滞肢体麻木是否持续

parameters.en: Neurologic recovery without recurrent seizure or agitation
parameters.zh: 神经功能恢复且癫痫或躁动不再复发

parameters.en: Size of the needle puncture mark
parameters.zh: 针刺痕迹大小

correct.en: The rapid sequence of metallic taste, tinnitus, CNS excitation/seizure, hypotension, and wide-complex dysrhythmia after local anesthetic exposure is classic for LAST. Treatment differs from routine ACLS and includes immediate cessation, specialized rescue activation, airway and seizure management, and early 20% lipid emulsion. Monitor cardiovascular stability and neurologic recovery.
correct.zh: 局麻药暴露后迅速出现金属味、耳鸣、中枢神经兴奋/癫痫、低血压和宽QRS心律失常，是LAST的典型表现。其复苏不同于常规ACLS，包括立即停药、启动专门救援、气道和癫痫处理以及尽早给予20%脂肪乳。应监测心血管稳定和神经功能恢复。

byChoice.en: The neurologic prodrome followed by cardiovascular collapse soon after the block strongly indicates LAST.
byChoice.zh: 阻滞后不久出现神经前驱症状并继发心血管崩溃，强烈提示LAST。

byChoice.en: Malignant hyperthermia is associated with hypermetabolism, rigidity, rising carbon dioxide, and hyperthermia rather than this classic local-anesthetic prodrome.
byChoice.zh: 恶性高热通常表现为高代谢、肌强直、二氧化碳升高和高热，而不是这种典型局麻药前驱症状。

byChoice.en: Anaphylaxis does not explain the characteristic metallic taste, tinnitus, seizure, and wide-complex sequence as well as LAST.
byChoice.zh: 过敏性休克不能像LAST那样解释特征性的金属味、耳鸣、癫痫和宽QRS演变。

byChoice.en: Seizure and cardiovascular instability are not expected block effects.
byChoice.zh: 癫痫和心血管不稳定不是阻滞的预期作用。

byChoice.en: Stopping further exposure and mobilizing the dedicated rescue pathway are immediate priorities.
byChoice.zh: 停止进一步暴露并启动专门救援流程是首要行动。

byChoice.en: Airway/seizure care and early 20% lipid emulsion are central LAST treatments.
byChoice.zh: 气道/癫痫处理和尽早给予20%脂肪乳是LAST治疗核心。

byChoice.en: ASRA warns that LAST resuscitation differs from standard ACLS; routine doses can be harmful.
byChoice.zh: ASRA警告LAST复苏不同于标准ACLS；常规剂量可能有害。

byChoice.en: The client has seizures and cardiovascular instability, so observation alone is unsafe.
byChoice.zh: 患者已有癫痫和心血管不稳定，单纯观察不安全。

byChoice.en: Additional local anesthetic worsens the toxic exposure.
byChoice.zh: 继续给予局麻药会加重毒性暴露。

byChoice.en: Ambulation is unsafe during seizure and hemodynamic instability.
byChoice.zh: 癫痫和血流动力学不稳定时下床活动不安全。

byChoice.en: Rhythm and blood pressure show whether cardiovascular toxicity is resolving.
byChoice.zh: 心律和血压显示心血管毒性是否缓解。

byChoice.en: Neurologic recovery and absence of recurrent seizures evaluate CNS resolution.
byChoice.zh: 神经功能恢复和无癫痫复发可评价中枢神经毒性是否缓解。

byChoice.en: Expected regional numbness is not the primary recovery target after systemic toxicity.
byChoice.zh: 区域麻木属于预期阻滞效应，不是全身毒性后的主要恢复指标。

byChoice.en: Taste is not a meaningful resuscitation outcome.
byChoice.zh: 味觉不是有意义的复苏结果。

byChoice.en: The puncture mark does not evaluate systemic toxicity resolution.
byChoice.zh: 针刺痕迹不能评价全身毒性是否缓解。

sourceMetadata: American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine (ASRA), Checklist for Treatment of Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity (LAST), including calling for help, airway/seizure support, early 20% lipid emulsion, modified resuscitation, and post-stability observation: https://asra.com/docs/default-source/guidelines-articles/local-anesthetic-systemic-toxicity-rgb.pdf

stem.en: A peritoneal-dialysis client reports new cloudy effluent and abdominal pain but is hemodynamically stable. The unit pathway requires this sequence: notify the PD clinician; obtain effluent for cell count with differential, Gram stain, and culture before the first antibiotic dose when doing so will not cause a dangerous delay; begin the prescribed empiric therapy promptly; then reassess symptoms, effluent clarity, and results for regimen adjustment. Place the actions in order.
stem.zh: 一名腹膜透析患者出现新的混浊透出液和腹痛，但血流动力学稳定。科室流程规定顺序为：通知腹透临床医生；在不会造成危险延误时，于首次抗生素给药前采集透出液进行细胞计数及分类、革兰染色和培养；立即开始医嘱经验性治疗；随后重新评估症状、透出液清晰度和结果，以调整方案。请按顺序排列行动。

options.en: Begin the prescribed empiric therapy promptly after specimens are obtained.
options.zh: 采集标本后立即开始医嘱经验性治疗。

options.en: Notify the PD clinician of suspected peritonitis.
options.zh: 通知腹透临床医生疑似腹膜炎。

options.en: Obtain PD effluent for cell count with differential, Gram stain, and culture before the first antibiotic dose, because this can be done without dangerous delay.
options.zh: 在不会造成危险延误的情况下，于首次抗生素给药前采集腹透液进行细胞计数及分类、革兰染色和培养。

options.en: Reassess symptoms and effluent clarity and review results for adjustment of the regimen.
options.zh: 重新评估症状和透出液清晰度，并审阅结果以调整方案。

correct.en: Cloudy effluent with abdominal pain requires prompt evaluation for PD peritonitis. Under the pathway stated in the stem for a stable client, notify the PD clinician, collect the specified effluent studies before the first antibiotic dose without dangerous delay, start prescribed empiric therapy promptly, and then reassess clinical response and results to refine treatment.
correct.zh: 混浊透出液伴腹痛需要迅速评估腹透相关腹膜炎。针对病情稳定的患者，按照题干给出的流程，应先通知腹透临床医生，在不造成危险延误的情况下于首次抗生素前采集指定透出液检查，然后立即开始医嘱经验性治疗，最后根据临床反应和结果调整治疗。

byChoice.en: Empiric therapy should begin promptly after microbiologic specimens are obtained.
byChoice.zh: 微生物标本采集后应立即开始经验性治疗。

byChoice.en: Clinical response and laboratory results are evaluated after treatment begins to guide adjustment.
byChoice.zh: 治疗开始后再评价临床反应和实验室结果，以指导调整。

byChoice.en: The unit pathway begins by activating the responsible PD clinician.
byChoice.zh: 科室流程首先要求通知负责的腹透临床医生。

byChoice.en: Appropriate effluent specimens should be collected before antibiotics when this does not create dangerous delay.
byChoice.zh: 在不会造成危险延误时，应在抗生素前采集适当透出液标本。

sourceMetadata: International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis (ISPD), Peritonitis guideline recommendations: 2022 update, diagnostic recommendations for PD effluent cell count/differential, Gram stain, and culture and recommendation to start empiric antibiotics as soon as possible after appropriate microbiologic specimens are obtained: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/08968608221080586

stem.en: A hospital is under a municipal boil-water advisory and has activated its emergency water plan. Highlight the actions consistent with the plan. Apply restrictions according to the intended use and patient risk; do not assume every possible use of tap water is prohibited.
stem.zh: 医院所在市政区域发布了煮沸用水警示，医院已启动紧急供水计划。请标出符合计划的行动。应根据用水目的和患者风险实施限制，不要假设所有自来水用途都被禁止。

segments.en: Stop using tap water and ordinary ice for drinking; provide bottled or appropriately disinfected water.
segments.zh: 停止使用自来水和普通冰块饮用，提供瓶装水或经过适当消毒的水。

segments.en: Use water that meets the emergency plan’s safe-water requirements for wound care.
segments.zh: 伤口护理使用符合紧急计划安全水要求的水。

segments.en: Use safe water for equipment and procedures identified in the emergency water plan.
segments.zh: 对紧急供水计划指定的设备和操作使用安全水。

segments.en: Notify patients, visitors, and affected departments about the advisory and approved water sources.
segments.zh: 通知患者、访客和受影响部门有关警示及获准使用的水源。

segments.en: Suspend sterile processing if the required water quality cannot be supplied.
segments.zh: 如果无法提供所需水质，应暂停无菌处理。

segments.en: Continue serving ice made from the building’s untreated water system.
segments.zh: 继续供应由建筑内未经处理的供水系统制成的冰。

segments.en: Announce that tap water is forbidden for every use, regardless of the task or patient population.
